cases.question: At what temperature does a box go critical?

good.answer: A box goes critical when its temperature reading is 55 C or higher. It is elevated at 48 C and a watch at 40 C.

bad.answer: A box goes critical at 70 C.

cases.question: How deep does the water reading have to be before it is critical?

good.answer: Water depth at the sensor is critical at 20 mm or more, elevated at 10 mm and a watch at 5 mm. A water detected signal is critical by itself.

bad.answer: Any water is fine until it floods the room.

cases.question: After how long without a report is a box offline, and is that an emergency?

good.answer: A box silent for more than 15 minutes is offline. Offline alone is never critical and never normal, so the home status is unknown.

bad.answer: After 5 minutes the box is offline and critical.
Offline means the box is normal.

cases.question: What carbon monoxide readings trigger each level?

good.answer: Carbon monoxide is a watch at 35 ppm, elevated at 70 ppm and critical at 150 ppm. The box is not a certified CO alarm.

cases.question: When is the backup battery reading flagged?

good.answer: Battery is a watch at 40 percent or less and elevated at 20 percent or less. With mains off and battery 30 percent or less the box is elevated.

bad.answer: The battery is only flagged at 5 percent.

cases.question: What are the priority tiers and what does P1 mean?

good.answer: P1 is a score of 80 or more and means review now. P2 starts at 40 and means check soon. P3 is routine.

cases.question: How old can a reading be on the map card before it counts as stale?

good.answer: The command-center card treats a box as stale when its newest reading is more than 300 seconds old, which is five minutes. A stale card is unknown unless it is critical.

cases.question: How long can an operator message to a box be?

good.answer: A title can be up to 20 characters and the body up to 80, in plain keyboard characters with no links.

bad.answer: Messages can be 500 characters with links.

cases.question: What are the saver and normal power profiles?

good.answer: Normal samples every 2 seconds and reports every 30 seconds. Saver samples every 2 seconds, reports every 120 seconds and retries Wi-Fi every 300 seconds. These are proposals, not applied to hardware, and alarms are never shed.

bad.answer: Saver turns the alarm off to save battery.
